rows.medi_said: [speaking foreign language] (engine lost it; Amal 19:13: 'cuz I heard آخر اليوم')
rows.amal_said: No. يمكن آخر يوم أو اليوم الأخير.
rows.why: aa5er + el- means 'the end of'; he meant 'the last day', Amal said No and gave aa5er yoam / el-yoam el-a5eer (engine lost his Arabic; her 19:13 'I heard آخر اليوم' shows what he said).
rows.english: Today is the last day (for taxes).

rows.medi_said: لا الـ tax. الـ مال، دي كذا ماليات؟ ... Do you guys say ماليات؟
rows.why: He used ماليات (Farsi maliyat = tax; Arabic 'finances') for taxes; Amal asked شو يعني and gave ضرايب.

rows.medi_said: الضرايب. Okay. Uh, آخر يوم الضرايب.
rows.why: Amal recast inserting لـ (for) between 'last day' and 'the taxes'; he then repeats her la- at 19:08.

rows.medi_said: It's آخر اليوم الضرايب.
rows.amal_said: آخر يوم لـ الضرايب. لـ الضرايب.
rows.why: After her 18:07 and 19:06 fixes he said آخر اليوم الضرايب again and she fixed it again (own slip per GR-32); low because he may be quoting what she heard.

rows.medi_said: اليوم، uh, يوم الـ أربع، uh, أربعين،
rows.why: He fumbled Wednesday (el-arbi3a) into أربع / أربعين (forty); Amal said أربعة and her chat writes yoam el-arbi3a; low because her أربعة could also be a nudge toward 14 (arba3ta3sh).

rows.medi_said: So أنا عندي مع شجرة... (engine for متشجع)
rows.amal_said: لا، لا، متأكدة is motivated (engine for متشجع)
rows.why: Amal had just said the noun 'motivation' exists (20:56); he put the adjective mitshajje3 after 3indi, she said no, mitshajje3 is 'motivated', and he switched to 7aafez (engine 'office') at 21:07, which she accepted; engine wrote مع شجرة / متأكدة for mitshajje3.
rows.english: I have motivation / I am motivated

rows.medi_said: كان عندي سنة ماضي و متحمس
rows.amal_said: What do you mean كان عندي سنة ماضية؟
rows.why: سنة is feminine; Amal echoed his phrase with ماضية and he used ماضية at 23:59.

rows.medi_said: أنا كان عندي سنة، س-سنة ماضية مني. I had a good last year.
rows.amal_said: No. That doesn't work like this. You could say my year was good. This year was good for me.
rows.wrong: أنا كان عندي سنة ماضية منيحة
rows.right: السنة كانت منيحة معي (my year was good / this year was good for me)
rows.why: Amal said No, Arabic doesn't 'have' a year; the period is the subject that 'was good'. No bucket covers this structure.
rows.english: I had a good year last year.
rows.proposed_rule: A period that went well is the subject, not something you 'have': el-sane kaanet mnee7a (ma3i), not kaan 3indi sane mnee7a (Amal: 'my year was good / this year was good for me').
